title: CA-ZTCF: Coexistence-Aware Zero Trust Continuity Framework
description:
A service-domain Zero Trust continuity function that re-evaluates IoT device trust at 5G/WiFi access transitions, using only evidence each access domain can realistically expose and without any cross-domain identifier sharing. Trust is derived by a criteria-based, contextual algorithm in the sense of NIST SP 800-207 §3.3.1: eleven named predicates over a versioned evidence record, an ordered rule system, six trust states and a transition-aware policy matrix. No weights, no scores, no machine learning, so every decision is explainable and exactly replayable.

This record carries the frozen experimental evidence for a master's thesis in Computer Networks Engineering: 2160 valid runs across fifteen scenarios, three decision strategies and thirty paired repetitions, plus a token-lifetime sensitivity analysis of the static-continuity baseline. The experiment protocol was frozen and committed before the first run; every attempt is recorded in a run ledger; and all processed data, tables, figures and statistics regenerate from the raw output.

Scope. The evaluation runs on a reproducible software-based 5G/WiFi coexistence testbed: Open5GS with UERANSIM for real 5G NAS, NGAP and GTP-U, and mac80211_hwsim with hostapd and wpa_supplicant for a real IEEE 802.11 association and EAP-TLS exchange. Both radios are simulated. The results support claims about authentication and session behaviour, access transitions, trust continuity, policy enforcement, application continuity, software latency, overhead and logical-device scalability up to 25 devices. They do not support any claim about RF propagation, physical radio handover, interference, signal strength, spectrum efficiency, channel quality or production mobile-network performance.
